implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing discs on an 8x8 grid
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.__init__ sets self.current_player = BLACK and Game._advance_turn switches to the opponent after each successful move (board.opponent). BOARD_SIZE = 8 in constants.py.
Board.is_valid_move uses Board.get_flips; Board.get_valid_moves iterates the whole board. Console and GUI call Game.get_valid_moves which forwards to Board.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flip opponent discs that are enclosed by the new disc
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board._flips_in_direction collects opponent discs and returns them only if bounded by a player disc; Board.place_disc flips all returned positions.
Board.get_score returns a dict of counts; Game.get_score forwards it. console.format_board and gui.draw_sidebar render the scores.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game when the board is full or no valid moves remain
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._advance_turn checks has_valid_move for both players; if neither can move, it calls _end_game which sets game_over. A full board yields no valid moves, so the same path ends the game.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Automatically pass a player who has no valid moves
implemented_requirements.evidence: In Game._advance_turn, if the opponent has no valid move but the current player still does, the message indicates a pass and current_player stays the same.

judge.summary: The repository provides a complete Reversi implementation. The Board class encodes all game rules (move validation, disc flipping, scoring). Game orchestrates turn order, automatic passing, and end‑game detection. Both a pygame GUI (gui.py) and a text console fallback (console.py) display the board and scores. No missing core functionality or stub code is observed, and the code appears ready to run (pygame optional).
